key_insight: An ancilla’s state ensembles change non-analytically at the measurement-induced purification transition, revealing changes in quantum-state randomness that their maximally mixed first moments cannot detect.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest higher-order ensemble diagnostics can reveal how hybrid quantum circuits distribute control over subsystem states between circuit measurements and final readout.
method: Study an ancilla entangled with a system evolving under unitary gates and projective measurements.
Compare trajectory ensembles conditioned on circuit outcomes with projected ensembles generated by additional final-time system measurements.
Analyse ensemble transitions and quantum-design properties in Haar-random and Clifford circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coincident ensemble and purification transitions: Haar-random trajectory ensembles change from identity to Haar, while projected ensembles change from Haar to a singleton pure state.
watch_item: Gate-set restrictions matter: Clifford projected ensembles reach only a 1-design, and the abstract provides no hardware validation or finite-size error estimates.
paper_title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
